uncertainty: Independent human-readable proof review accepts completeness only within explicitly maintained model classes; no Lean or other proof kernel verification was performed. General nonlinear lottery preferences, unrestricted waiting preferences, exact-zero discount factors and exhaustive equal-cost/boundary characterization remain outside scope.

claim_reviews.weakest_link: The one-sentence question leaves waiting preferences underdetermined; the manuscript expressly adds sufficient model restrictions.
claim_reviews.scope_or_number_mismatch: No silent generalization from contractive, discount or additive models to all waiting preferences.
claim_reviews.competing_explanation: Different waiting-cost functions can change uniqueness and delay; this is explicitly demonstrated.

claim_reviews.weakest_link: Model primitives, feasible pie, complete public histories, terminal utility, disagreement and whole-continuation SPE deviations are stated.
claim_reviews.scope_or_number_mismatch: Pure nonlinear delay maps are separated from behavioral expected-utility models.
claim_reviews.competing_explanation: Outside options, breakdown, incomplete information and indivisibilities would define different games and are excluded.

claim_reviews.weakest_link: Appendix A.2 constructs the fixed point, proves interiority and checks every finite or infinite pure deviation. The infimum/supremum envelopes range over all pure SPE and histories; contraction collapses payoff spans without assuming stationary equilibrium.
claim_reviews.scope_or_number_mismatch: Complete paper proof within strictly increasing Lipschitz delay maps with q_i in (0,1); no lottery-utility extension is claimed.
claim_reviews.competing_explanation: Noncontractive maps could preserve equilibrium payoff spans. This possibility is outside the theorem.

claim_reviews.weakest_link: Appendix A.3 checks pathwise payoffs for arbitrary behavioral deviations, bounds expected payoff feasibility, collapses both equilibrium payoff spans and forces deterministic offers and threshold ties at every history.
claim_reviews.scope_or_number_mismatch: The algebra yields the two proposer-role shares, not a single division. Behavioral strategies with defined measurable laws are the stated scope; kernel verification is absent.
claim_reviews.competing_explanation: History dependence and positive-probability mixing cannot escape the stated envelope and strict rejection-payoff gap.

claim_reviews.weakest_link: The strict positive gap p_i-delta_i(1-p_j) makes any positive rejection probability incompatible with the established proposer payoff.
claim_reviews.scope_or_number_mismatch: Immediate acceptance is proved in every finite proposer subgame only for strict positive discount factors.
claim_reviews.competing_explanation: A perfectly patient player can be indifferent to finite delay, which the separate boundary construction permits.

claim_reviews.weakest_link: Appendix A.4 verifies denominator positivity, quotient-rule signs, symmetry and the ratio of first-order exponential limits.
claim_reviews.scope_or_number_mismatch: Positive r_i are maintained, and the limit is expressly a limit of discrete equilibria rather than a continuous-time existence theorem.
claim_reviews.competing_explanation: Changing how rates or period costs scale could produce different limiting games.

claim_reviews.weakest_link: Appendix A.5 proves nonnegative equilibrium continuation payoffs and finite expected waiting before using feasibility. Its clipped-reservation envelopes force the lower-cost proposer value to one; the strict rejection gap then proves behavioral strategy and timing uniqueness.
claim_reviews.scope_or_number_mismatch: Positive unequal costs and the both-at-least-one case are covered, including equality at one. Actual negative rejection values force strict acceptance of zero rather than artificial indifference.
claim_reviews.competing_explanation: Equal costs below one do not satisfy the strict-composite inequality and are expressly excluded from global uniqueness.

claim_reviews.weakest_link: Appendix A.6 derives the two clipped reservation equations for stationary immediate behavioral equilibria and solves them in both clipping cases; existence follows from the prior complete deviation checks.
claim_reviews.scope_or_number_mismatch: The interval p1 in [c,1] and p2=1-p1+c characterizes only the stationary immediate family.
claim_reviews.competing_explanation: Other history-dependent equal-cost equilibria may exist and are not ruled out.

claim_reviews.weakest_link: The initial-offer-dependent B/P continuations are SPE at every later history. Every y=0, 0<y<0.9 and y>=0.9 response and proposer deviation is checked; utilities 0.7 and 0.1 sum to 0.8 after one rejection.
claim_reviews.scope_or_number_mismatch: One explicit equal-cost c=0.1 existence example, not an exhaustive delayed-equilibrium characterization.
claim_reviews.competing_explanation: Continuation-equilibrium selection supports delay; the construction does not rely on an unspecified noncredible punishment.

claim_reviews.weakest_link: Appendix A.7 specifies calendar-date strategies for every finite K and all histories. The patient player attains its payoff upper bound; the other player cannot earn a positive share. Both-patient fixed divisions also survive complete deviations.
claim_reviews.scope_or_number_mismatch: Finite-delay existence is claimed, not boundary uniqueness. Exact-zero discounts and zero-cost additive uniqueness are excluded.
claim_reviews.competing_explanation: Indifference at perfectly patient threshold ties permits timing multiplicity.

external_results_status: Listed elementary real-analysis and expectation facts accepted as external results; no bargaining or infinite-game existence theorem imported.
